essen-ruhr.title: Southern Essen / Ruhr, NRW DGM1
essen-ruhr.notes: 10.24 km regional tile; source is bare terrain, not water depth or buildings.

ruhr-wide.title: Ruhr regional expansion, NRW DGM1
ruhr-wide.notes: 20.48 km regional expansion, not all NRW.

drachenfels.title: Drachenfels / Siebengebirge, NRW DGM1
drachenfels.notes: 5.12 km terrain contrast. Nodata across service/state boundaries is refused, not filled.

muensterland-plain.title: Münsterland plain (Coesfeld basin), NRW DGM1
muensterland-plain.notes: Flattest arm of the multi-region relief ladder: 25.2 m relief, 2.74 m std over 10.24 km. Ground-moraine lowland; drainage is engineered and low-gradient, so the D8 network here is the hardest of the six to reproduce and the easiest to get accidentally right.

coverage_probe.note: Full 10.24 km extent probed at SCALEFACTOR 0.025 before acquisition; every node returned real terrain. The same probe rejected the eifel-uplands candidate at 7.86% nodata, where the tile crosses into Belgium. The prepare step refuses any nodata, so probing first avoids a download that would fail.

lower-rhine.title: Lower Rhine floodplain (Wesel), NRW DGM1
lower-rhine.notes: Near-matched in roughness to Münsterland but a different process: fluvial terraces and cut-off meanders rather than glacial till. The pair is the same-relief/different-process control that a relief ladder alone cannot supply.

coverage_probe.note: Full 10.24 km extent probed at SCALEFACTOR 0.025 before acquisition. The probe reported 0.00% nodata, but it decimates 40:1; acquisition at full spacing found a 6x6 hole (24 of 1,050,625 nodes, 0.002%) near the north edge at E 322960-323010, N 5725980-5726030. The tile sits one page (640 m) south of that hole to exclude it, which keeps the lattice on the same underlying grid. A decimated probe cannot certify that a region is free of nodata; it can only reject one, as it did for eifel-uplands (7.86% nodata where the tile crosses into Belgium).

teutoburg-forest.title: Teutoburg Forest ridge, NRW DGM1
teutoburg-forest.notes: A single narrow strike ridge crossing the tile: strongly anisotropic and structurally controlled, where an isotropic prior should visibly fail.
